The course meets its objectives of providing a broad survey of key issues in international security. She also takes time to recap and remind students, who may not be from IR, of various IR theories as important lenses to analyses international security issues. Prof provides safe opportunities for students to try out and practise making arguments that are theoretically-supported and example-driven in class discussions. As an exchange student who has never done a spontaneous debate before, the exercise was memorable, exhilarating and beneficial in enhancing my thinking skills. She may also want to make it a blanket rule for students to use Word document to record their answers before pasting them on Moodle. Giving too many options for students is confusing and telling them these options in the midst of the exams themselves causes unnecessary stress. But, overall, this course, being my first ever IR course, has stimulated my interest in taking other IR-related courses in my home university and I will be sure to use what I have learnt in other IR courses in future!

The problem is, I have other research papers also, and I gave similar evaluations for them. I start to shape my research paper after the first half of the semester since I become more knowledgeable on the subject. But courses that expect research papers, put deadlines on 5th or 6th weeks.
